vocabulary.meaning_en: to begin (a journey, job or business)
vocabulary.example: He started out with one small shop.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to finally be in a place or situation you didn't plan or expect
vocabulary.example: We got lost and ended up in a small village.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to grow bigger by adding parts over time; to accumulate
vocabulary.example: I've built up a big collection of books.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to collect more and more of something over time
to slowly become less strong or loud
vocabulary.example: The wind died down in the evening.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to suddenly become unconscious; also to give things out to people
vocabulary.note_ar: معنيان: يفقد الوعي، ويوزّع (pass out the tests)
vocabulary.note_en: Two meanings: faint, or hand out.
vocabulary.example: It was so hot on the bus that a man passed out.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to become conscious again; also to add up to a total
vocabulary.note_ar: لا نقول come to عن الاستيقاظ العادي بل wake up
vocabulary.note_en: For normal sleep say wake up, not come to.
vocabulary.example: When he came to, he was in hospital. / That comes to $5.50.

vocabulary.meaning_en: not awake and not able to see or feel, e.g. after an accident
vocabulary.example: She was unconscious for a few minutes.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to persuade someone NOT to do something
vocabulary.example: I talked my brother out of quitting school.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to persuade someone TO do something
vocabulary.example: The salesman talked me into buying an expensive jacket.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to feel sorry about something you did
vocabulary.example: I bought it, and now I regret it.

fine_lines.title: start out vs end up
fine_lines.explanation_ar: start out = تبدأ. end up = تصل في النهاية إلى مكان أو موقف لم تخطّط له.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Start out = begin. End up = finally arrive somewhere you didn't plan.

examples.sentence: We ended up at the wrong restaurant.

fine_lines.title: build up vs die down
fine_lines.explanation_ar: build up = يكبر ويزداد. die down = يصغر ويخفت تدريجيًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Build up = grow bigger. Die down = slowly get smaller or quieter.

examples.sentence: The noise died down after the speech.

fine_lines.title: pass out vs come to
fine_lines.explanation_ar: pass out = يُغمى عليه فجأة (حرّ، رؤية الدم...). come to = يستعيد وعيه بعد الإغماء. للنوم العادي نقول fall asleep / wake up.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Pass out = suddenly become unconscious (heat, seeing blood...). Come to = become conscious again. For normal sleep, say fall asleep / wake up.

examples.sentence: My mother passes out when she sees blood.
She came to after a few seconds.

fine_lines.title: talk out of vs talk into
fine_lines.explanation_ar: talk someone out of = تقنعه ألّا يفعل. talk someone into = تقنعه أن يفعل.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Talk someone out of = persuade them not to do it. Talk someone into = persuade them to do it.

examples.sentence: My father talked me out of buying a motorbike.
My friend talked me into joining the gym.

expressions.example: The bread is $3.50 and the water is $2. That comes to $5.50.

expressions.meaning_en: Please give the tests to everyone.
expressions.example: Can you pass out the books, please?
I ended up staying at home.

grammar.title: Phrasal verbs can have several meanings
grammar.explanation_ar: الفعل المركّب الواحد قد يحمل أكثر من معنى، والسياق يحدده: pass out = يُغمى عليه أو يوزّع؛ come to = يستعيد وعيه أو يبلغ مجموعًا؛ pick up = يلتقط أو يُقِلّ أو يلتقط إشارة.
grammar.explanation_en: One phrasal verb can have several meanings; context decides: pass out = faint / hand out; come to = wake after fainting / add up to; pick up = lift / collect someone / receive a signal.
examples: He passed out from the heat.
The teacher passed out the papers.

questions.question: Which means "to come to a place that was not planned"?
questions.explanation_ar: end up = ينتهي به المطاف في مكان غير مخطط.

questions.question: Which means "to accumulate by putting parts together"?
Which means "to stop someone doing something by talking about reasons not to"?
questions.explanation_ar: talk someone out of = يقنعه ألا يفعل.
questions.explanation_en: Talk out of = persuade not to.

questions.question: "The salesman ___ me ___ buying an expensive car."
questions.explanation_ar: talk someone into = يقنعه أن يفعل.

questions.question: "It was very hot, and a woman on the bus ___."
"Can you ___ the tests, please?" (give to everyone)
After a normal night's sleep, you ___.
questions.explanation_ar: بعد النوم العادي نقول wake up.
questions.explanation_en: After normal sleep, you wake up.
